Devil Fruits are supernatural fruits that each grant a unique power when eaten, at the cost of removing the eater's ability to swim. A Devil Fruit power can only be held by one individual at a time, but will reappear in a new fruit after they die. In turn, no individual may acquire more than one power, with only one historic exception.

Devil Fruits exist along three broad categories: Paramecia, the most common, which grant a vast array of "superhuman" abilities; Zoan, which grant the power to transform into animals; and Logia, the rarest and most powerful, which grant the power to transform into a natural element. Each fruit has a unique appearance, making identification and documentation possible, although there is at least one known case of a fruit being renamed and rebranded.

Scattered throughout the world, Devil Fruits are rare enough to be considered myths in much of the Blue Seas. They appear to be most common in the Grand Line, having empowered many key figures among the Three Great Powers. This rarity, coupled with their abilities, make Devil Fruits highly sought-after; some specimens may sell for billions, and extensive efforts have been made to replicate their powers and mass-produce artificial versions for warfare. The scientist Vegapunk has performed the most extensive research into Devil Fruits and achieved many unnatural applications and replications of their abilities, but not even he knows their origins for certain.

Overview Origins Currently, almost nothing on the origins, mechanics, or true nature of Devil Fruits is known for certain. Even the world's greatest scientist, Dr. Vegapunk, has at most speculated they are a manifestation of various possibilities for human evolution, with all the different powers representing the many branches for humanity's future, brought into existence by human hope and desire: thoughts along the lines of "if only I could do this" or "if only I could be like that". Vegapunk claims that those with powers exist in different dimensions dreamed up by others before them. However, according to Vegapunk, those who exist in this unnatural state are loathed by the sea, which he describes as the mother of nature, and thus become unable to swim as punishment.

Other legends state that Devil Fruits were enchanted by "sea devils". Another theory was that they are inhabited by actual devils which fight each other if they get too close, though this was eventually debunked by science.

What is definitely known is that Devil Fruits have existed in the world for at least eight centuries, with the oldest known fruits being the Toki Toki no Mi and the Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika. There are more than 100 different Devil Fruits in the world, but only one of each Devil Fruit exists.

As mentioned, each Devil Fruit has a unique appearance, with the only commonality being their distinctly swirl-patterned skins. Some have mundane shapes akin to ordinary fruits, while others have highly unusual shapes reflecting their respective powers: for example, the Gomu Gomu no Mi has the shape of a regular , while the Mera Mera no Mi is shaped (and colored) like a flame. In at least one case, that of the Sara Sara no Mi, Model: Axolotl, the Devil Fruit greatly resembled the apple that became it, implying that the base fruit may play a role in the Devil Fruit’s appearance. In addition, Devil Fruits do not rot over time like regular fruits, and can last for centuries, as exemplified by the Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Nidhöggr, which was kept in a chest for centuries without any signs of decay.
In contrast, Artificial Devil Fruits bear ring-patterned skins rather than swirls, and in many cases have identical shapes, reflecting their mass-produced nature.

On the very first bite, a Devil Fruit will bestow a superpower or a special superhuman trait that stays with the eater for life; no method of withdrawing these powers is known, save for death. The effect occurs immediately after the eater swallows, apparently without needing conventional digestion (though the eater may need time to discover what the powers actually are). After the first bite has been taken and the consumer gains its power, any remainders of the fruit become powerless.

Devil Fruits are universally known to taste very bad, though the exact degree may possibly vary by fruit (or the eater's personal standards). While this taste remains in even a powerless fruit, some will choose to eat the entire fruit regardless.

Those empowered by Devil Fruits are popularly known as . Many other descriptors have also been coined for users of specific powers, usually a simple combination of the power and the user's identity, e.g., for the Gomu Gomu-powered Luffy, or for the Hito Hito-powered Chopper, though more poetic titles also exist, e.g., for the Kage Kage no Mi's user.

Consuming a Devil Fruit is known to alter the user's Lineage Factor, and extracting this genetic blueprint has allowed scientists to make breakthroughs in replicating fruit powers. However, the user's altered Lineage Factor has not been shown to affect them beyond granting the fruit abilities and side-effects; all Devil Fruit users appear to retain normal lifespans, and remain capable of siring children who possess no powers and can eat their own Devil Fruits without hazard.

A person can only eat a single Devil Fruit in their entire lifetime; any attempt to gain a second Devil Fruit power will cause instant death, reportedly by a full-body explosion that leaves no remains. The reason for this is currently unknown; though Jabra believes that an actual devil inhabits each fruit and will fight to the death if put in close proximity, Blueno dismissed this as a rumor without scientific backing. The only apparent exception to this rule is Marshall D. Teach, who manages to hold the powers of both the Yami Yami no Mi and the Gura Gura no Mi without any visible consequences. Marco attributed this to Teach's body being "odd," but this has yet to be elaborated on.

Certain methods exist for obtaining a Devil Fruit power outside of conventional eating. Charlotte Linlin had somehow obtained the power of the Soru Soru no Mi after its previous user, Carmel, disappeared, but it is unknown how she did it. In addition, it is possible for a sufficiently skilled scientist to create an extract of a Devil Fruit and administer it to an infant too young to eat solid food; this method results in the recipient gaining the ability as normal while the fruit becomes worthless, as if the baby had eaten the fruit normally.

Notably, Devil Fruit powers generally extend through the clothes the user wears. When a Devil Fruit user's body changes in size or shape, their clothing will stretch out and change with them without being any the worse for wear afterwards. When a Devil Fruit power involves the user's body changing in nature, that power also applies to their clothing, which will change in nature with them. If a power involves generating a substance, then it can come from the user's clothing. This rule also applies to cyborg enhancements and prosthetic body parts. An example of this is Queen's artificial arm, which transforms into a brachiosaurus leg when he takes his brachiosaurus form. However, it would seem that not all Devil Fruit powers adhere to this rule. Jewelry Bonney is an example, whose clothes do not change when her body does. That said, the change may extend to weapons or other items on the user's direct person as well, such as Sasaki's sword, Karakuri Rasento, growing in size in his hand when he transformed into a huge triceratops hybrid.
Types of Devil Fruit All Devil Fruits are categorized along three basic based on the nature of the powers they grant: Paramecia, Zoan, and Logia.

Paramecia, the most common Devil Fruit type, encompasses fruits that grant any one of a wide variety of "superhuman" abilities. By far the broadest Devil Fruit class, the one unifying characteristic of Paramecia fruits is that they are anything other than the ability to transform into animals or into elements of nature.

Some Paramecia fruits allow one to transform oneself or adopt a special bodily trait, temporarily or permanently (e.g., gaining a slippery physique, a body that can split into pieces harmlessly, a diamond body, becoming a jacket to be worn by others, transforming into blades and other weapons, controlling one's weight, mimicking appearances, gaining clairvoyant eyes or a brain with infinite storage capacity, etc.).

Other abilities involve creating (usually non-naturally occurring) substances from nothing, some of which may have unnatural properties, such as: wax as hard as steel, soap that "cleans off" strength, poison, strings that control people like puppets, straw with "voodoo" properties, arrows that control motion, invisible thorns, etc. Other fruits' powers involve creating and manipulating intangible forces (like "quake" shockwaves, gravity, or heat) and yet other abilities involve summoning discrete objects or entities (e.g., copies of one's own body parts, ghosts, a "genie" familiar, articles of clothing, etc.).

Still other Paramecia powers allow wielders to influence and alter their environment, both living beings (sometimes including the user themself) and/or objects, e.g., turning people into toys, controlling people's shadows or souls, "taming" animals, controlling specific objects like books or mirrors, making things levitate, making projectiles auto-lock onto targets, "surgically" modifying anything within a set domain, etc.

Zoan-type Devil Fruits grant the power to transform into a specific animal, in addition to a hybrid form combining the user's own species (most frequently human) with the aforesaid animal's. Unlike other Devil Fruits, Zoan fruits are said to carry a will of their own. A recently discovered science allows Zoan Fruits to be "eaten" even by inanimate objects, bringing said objects to life with all the standard Zoan powers.

Zoan powers can greatly enhance one's physical abilities, and are said to be the best kind for melee combat, with carnivore Zoans being especially ideal due to their predatory attributes (claws, fangs, etc.). Some Zoans grant special abilities based on the animal, like avian Zoans granting the ability of flight, the king cobra Zoan allowing the user to spit deadly venom, or the mole Zoan allowing the user to dig through the earth—including solid bedrock—at high speed.

Aside from standard Zoans that transform users into common, extant animals, there are three known sub-classifications: Ancient Zoan Fruits allow the user to transform into an extinct species, such as dinosaurs. Ancient Zoans are rare, and they appear to be stronger than regular Zoans. Some have even displayed atypical physical abilities that their users claim the real animals naturally possessed. Mythical Zoan Fruits allow the user to transform into mythological creatures, such as a dragon or a phoenix. Mythical Zoan animals tend to have additional special powers, like a phoenix Zoan being able to generate flames that have healing powers. Mythical Zoans are the rarest type of Devil Fruit, even more so than Logias. Artificial Zoan Fruits cause the user to permanently take on an animal characteristic; though, much more rarely, the user becomes able to transform at will. The artificial Zoan Fruits had a 10% success rate, while the other 90%, in addition to not gaining animal traits and losing the ability to swim, were stripped of the ability to express negative emotions, leaving them only able to smile and laugh, regardless of how they actually feel. These artificial Devil Fruits, known as SMILEs, were developed by Caesar Clown and Donquixote Doflamingo. Another version was developed by Vegapunk.

Logia, the rarest and most powerful of the three basic Devil Fruit types, refers to fruits that grant the power to create, control, and transform one's body into an element of nature, e.g., fire, lightning, ice, sand, mud, magma, smoke, soot, snow, gas, plants, light, and darkness.

When transforming into their element, a Logia user becomes physically invulnerable (outright intangible, in the case of certain elements) and retains control over their body even if separated into pieces. A Logia user may also gain ancillary powers conceptually tied to their element, such as the sand Logia's power to drain moisture, the light Logia's ability to travel at light speed, the gas Logia's power to control the atmosphere, or the darkness Logia's power to nullify other Devil Fruit abilities on contact. The darkness Logia, in particular, stands out for its element being more esoteric compared to other Logias, representing not merely an absence of light but, rather, the all-consuming "darkness" of black holes. Some Logia powers even create a seemingly infinite space inside the user's elemental form.
Some few Logias that are considered non-canon grant the ability to become an artificial "element" like paper or candy syrup, although no such fruit has been introduced in the manga.

Canon Laffitte's unnamed Devil Fruit allows him to sprout angelic wings and utilize them to fly. Gunyo Gunyo no Mi (English versions: Glorp-Glorp Fruit): Allows the user to create and control clay. Eaten by Prince Grus. An unnamed Devil Fruit in the possession of a Panda Shark.

Akuma no Mi The Akuma no Mi is a fruit eaten by Nerona Imu, the King of the World who has lived for the last eight centuries. The fruit is notable for its unique name which forgoes the repeated two-syllable style possessed by all other Devil Fruits, and is homonymous with the term "Devil Fruit" itself. Though its name makes categorization with other fruits uncertain, it does possess many of the special traits of a Mythical Zoan fruit as its basic power is demonic transformation. Notably, the fruit's esoteric powers are accessible not just to the user, but to anyone the user brands with a Covenant.

Non-Canon Meta Meta no Mi: Allows the user to control liquid metal, making them a Liquid Metal Human (液体金属人間 Ekitai Kinzoku Ningen). It was eaten by Graydle. Zuma Zuma no Mi: Allows the user to control plasma, making the user a Plasma Human (プラズマ人間 Purazuma Ningen). It was eaten by Smash.

Instead of conventional growing, the ability simply takes hold of an existing, full-grown fruit, transforming it into the Devil Fruit both internally and externally.

Notably, unlike regular fruits, Devil Fruits do not rot. The Mera Mera no Mi was on the island of Sixis for years after a pirate crew shipwrecked there with it, and it was still completely fresh by the time Portgas D. Ace and Masked Deuce discovered it.

Artificial Devil Fruits SMILE Devil Fruits have been shown to grow on trees, groomed by the Dwarves of the Tontatta Kingdom under the Donquixote Pirates' coercion. Unlike natural Devil Fruits, the SMILE appear to begin as ordinary, powerless fruits that "ripen" into their abilities over time.
Also, unlike their natural counterparts, artificial Devil Fruits do not enter into circulation once a user dies.

The main attraction of eating a Devil Fruit is, of course, the power bestowed on the user. Some powers are good for support, such as healing others, enhancing the senses, and turning objects into food. Many of these powers are advantageous in combat, such as enhanced physical strength, various unique attacks, and even control over the forces of nature. More often than not, the benefits and uses bestowed by a Devil Fruit far outweigh the loss of the ability to swim, as stated by Blackbeard and Rob Lucci. Regardless of what power one receives, even ones that would normally be considered "weird" or "useless" can be utilized as a highly valuable asset both in and out of combat. If nothing else, eating a Devil Fruit will not weaken its user, as Rob Lucci noted. How strong a Devil Fruit itself is depends solely on its user's strength, skill, and creativity in how to use its power. Even users of seemingly weak Paramecia fruits can become powerhouses in their own right if they are proficient in using them; by contrast, a user of a Mythical Zoan or a Logia fruit can be easy to defeat as a result of the user having no combat training or underestimating their foes.

Devil Fruit powers are so varied and mysterious that the powers gained from eating one can serve purposes that may transcend normal limits. A good example of this is the Ope Ope no Mi, which has the title "Ultimate Devil Fruit", as it grants the user the miraculous power to cure any disease, including unknown and incurable diseases, in addition to being able to grant eternal life to anyone in exchange for the life of its user.

Additionally, since each Devil Fruit user possesses a unique ability, they each require different countermeasures, outside of the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses of Seastone and the inability to swim. As such, Devil Fruit users with odd or unfamiliar powers are very tricky to deal with in a fight. The standard approach is to take a step back and experiment with different means of attack against the Devil Fruit user. Another advantage of Devil Fruit powers is that many places and people lack information about them, resulting in the belief that the powers are some kind of magic or curse. The user can utilize these misconceptions on how the power was achieved to manipulate individuals for the user's purposes.
thumb|left|210px|A Wano Country citizen referring to their Paramecia power as a Jutsu.

Despite all the powers they may grant, Devil Fruits are not without downsides. One such downside is that so little is really known about them. In some cases, an entire society can be completely unaware of the existence of Devil Fruits. Due to this lack of information and with many Devil Fruits being unknown, eating a Devil Fruit can often be described as a "long shot", because on several occasions, it is only possible to know what type of Devil Fruit was after eating it and manifesting the power, which can often result in a power that is very difficult for the person to control.

Even if the power that a Devil Fruit user gains is useful, a Devil Fruit user does not automatically have control over their powers. All Devil Fruit users must train to learn how to activate, control, and use their power. This process could potentially put the Devil Fruit user in a painful and/or humiliating position.

Another downside is that, while many citizens can be fascinated by people with powers, others may consider a Devil Fruit user to be "a freak", "a monster", "a abomination" or even "a devil". With no way of removing the power, a Devil Fruit user may end up leading a miserable life full of discrimination and cruelty from those around them.

The effects of Devil Fruit powers can also be reversed or nullified by an opponent's Haki. However, the user must possess a very powerful level of Haki in order to accomplish this. This application of Haki has only been displayed by powerful New World fighters.
Weakness to Water thumb|210px|Submerged Devil Fruit users losing their strength.

The most universal drawback of eating a Devil Fruit is an immediate inability to swim, popularly called "becoming a . As the sea "hates" and rejects Devil Fruit users, the user will rapidly lose energy and muscle control when submerged in water, and become helpless to even stay afloat (though breathing or speech may continue if their mouth is not obstructed).
In a world comprised almost entirely of ocean, this weakness can prove deadly to many Devil Fruit users, especially pirates and Marines sailing the Grand Line.
thumb|left|210px|Devil Fruit users in bathwater, powerless but still able to move due to its relative shallowness.

The exact parameters of this weakness appear to be somewhat fluid, and may possibly vary by user. According to Nami, a user will begin losing strength once their body is half-submerged; however, this very observation was made of Kalifa, who showed no discomfort or immobility even when occupying a filled bathtub. On the other hand, both Luffy and Brook have been weakened simply by standing in thigh-deep water. Broadly, it appears that Devil Fruit users can submerge enough to safely bathe as long as their heads and at least some limbs remain exposed, though doing so still weakens them; notably, none have been seen activating their powers in this state.

If wholly (or near-wholly) submerged, users will swiftly become physically helpless, seemingly by dint of being rapidly weakened rather than something like being instantly paralyzed: Luffy, in particular, has been able to thrash at the surface and cry out for at least several seconds after falling into deep water. Still, no user has been known to escape this state without some form of outside help.

Overall, the vulnerability is not limited to seawater, as any sufficiently deep body of water can be considered an extension of the "sea." Thus, Devil Fruit users may be incapacitated by rivers, pools, and the Sea Clouds of Skypiea, among others. However, the water must be dense and enclosed enough to truly submerge a body: "scattered" water such as rain has no effects on Devil Fruit users, and they can shower without any hazard (save for specific cases such as the Suna Suna no Mi). Additionally, any Devil Fruit user can move underwater at full strength if enough of their body surface is kept airtight, e.g., with makeshift diving gear or Yarukiman Resin bubbles.

thumb|210px|Devil Fruit users can move freely underwater with properly airtight protection. (In this case, however, Luffy reported losing strength as more of his arm became directly exposed to the sea.)

Relatedly, many Devil Fruit powers—and their byproducts—can withstand and even directly affect water as long as the user is not incapacitated: for instance, the Doru Doru no Mi can easily create a shell of waterproof wax, and the Hie Hie no Mi can freeze paths over seawater that last for weeks. Moreover, some "passive" powers may still work even if the user is incapacitated: notably, a body turned rubber by the Gomu Gomu no Mi will remain so underwater, and can be stretched by outside forces (a fact that helped Genzo and Nojiko resuscitate Luffy after he was thrown into Arlong Park's harbor).

It should be noted that just being wet is not enough to induce weakness and nullify the user's powers; the same is true for water inside the Devil Fruit user's body, such as water that the user drinks, as seen when Luffy used Water Luffy: he and his powers were not affected in any way by the water in his body or the water covering his fists.

One of the greatest dangers created by a Devil Fruit user's weakness to water is the risk of drowning, which opponents can take advantage of in order to kill even the strongest of Devil Fruit users. The risk of drowning only applies to a Devil Fruit user if they cannot breathe underwater; as fish-man and merfolk Devil Fruit users are capable of breathing underwater, they are not subject to this risk. Even if a Devil Fruit user can survive underwater without drowning, they will still be rendered unable to move. This immobility would make such users vulnerable to underwater dangers, such as ocean predators, as they would be incapable of defending themselves.

On the other hand, some Devil Fruit powers are even more vulnerable to water than the norm, with mere contact being able to weaken, or even outright destroy their effects. Salt, considered to embody some of the powers of the sea, can also interfere with specific Devil Fruit abilities in certain circumstances.

In addition to the weakness to actual water, there is a substance known as Seastone: a special, near-indestructible substance that emits the same energy as the sea, referred to as the sea in solid form. Contact with Seastone has the same effect on Devil Fruit users as falling into the water, preventing the Devil Fruit user from using their powers and weakening the Devil Fruit user to the point where they cannot move. The Marines use this to their advantage when imprisoning pirates in Impel Down. However, a Devil Fruit user can resist and even ignore the weakening effect if they have enough physical endurance, and it has been indicated that a Devil Fruit user could resist the weakening effect of standing water in the same manner, as Sanjuan Wolf, while complaining of it still affecting him, was able to hold himself upright while standing chest deep in water. It is still unconfirmed whether such physical powerhouses would be able to actively use their Devil Fruit powers while exposed to such substances, as neither was shown attempting to trigger it in these situations.

While the strength and capabilities of a Devil Fruit are ultimately determined by the strength and skill of the user, some Devil Fruit powers interact in specific ways against each other, regardless of the user's capabilities. In some cases, one Devil Fruit has natural superiority over another, resulting in a significant advantage in combat. Aside from this rule of superiority, other Devil Fruit powers can react to each other in all kinds of unpredictable manners.

List of Confirmed Superiorities Some Devil Fruits of similar powers have been confirmed to be in a relationship of superiority and inferiority. In a fight between the two, the one with the superior power is almost certain to win. Though this in no way means that the user of the superior power is stronger than the inferior's user.

Eating a Devil Fruit will not automatically grant any level of knowledge or skill over its powers; to properly use them, a user must actively train themselves. Through training, a user can gain greater understanding of a given power's mechanics and limitations, enabling more versatile and efficient uses. Under enough proficiency, even fruits with seemingly harmless powers can become great assets in combat; the rare few that train their bodies to a fruit's full potential may even gain the additional powers of an Awakening (see below). On the other hand, those easily satisfied by basic powers and negligent of training will frequently waste the full potential of their Devil Fruits; in such hands, even the most fearsome powers may be practically useless.

(Of course, training potential can be severely limited if a user misunderstands their fruit's power. For instance, the World Government's public labeling of the Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika as the "Gomu Gomu no Mi" led Luffy to assume his powers were those of a common Paramecia, and training accordingly; Luffy would only unwittingly access Nika's higher powers well into the New World, and to this day remains unaware of his true nature as a Mythical Zoan.)
thumb|210px|Dracule Mihawk, a human lacking any Devil Fruit powers, defeats Daz Bonez, a Full-Body Bladed Human.

Of course, Devil Fruit users are never infallible against non-users, and even those with incredible powers can be surpassed by those with none: for instance, Roronoa Zoro has, purely on his own strength and skill, defeated the likes of Gem, Daz Bonez, Kaku, Monet, Pica, King and Rob Lucci in combat. Most famously, Gol D. Roger never ate a Devil Fruit in his lifetime, but wielded enough strength to rival Edward Newgate, whose powers could raise potentially world-splitting earthquakes (and were even reputed as "the Strongest Paramecia"); Roger went on to conquer the entire Grand Line and become Pirate King, a feat that, two decades after his death, remains unmatched even by Devil Fruit users as powerful as Charlotte Linlin, Kaidou, and Shiki. Some of Roger's crewmen rivaled his own strength, also without Devil Fruit powers, such as Silvers Rayleigh, Scopper Gaban, Kouzuki Oden, and Shanks. Other legendary and world-renowned figures who do not possess or have possessed Devil Fruit powers include Monkey D. Garp, Don Chinjao, Sanji, Jinbe, Dracule Mihawk, and Koby. According to Kaidou, Devil Fruit powers fall short of Haki in determining who can conquer the sea.

Different people take different amounts of time to master their powers. For example, Luffy spent years learning to use the Gomu Gomu no Mi, whereas Kalifa and Kaku only took hours to get used to their new abilities after consuming their Devil Fruits. Sabo trained with his Mera Mera no Mi ability at Baltigo days after Doflamingo's downfall, indicating that Sabo was still trying to understand its power. Despite having his devil fruit for a long time, it took Brook the recent 2 years purposely study his Yomi Yomi no Mi to finally understand its full potential, earning his title of Soul King.

Proficiency is also tied to the user's stamina. Before Chopper improved his Monster Point, he had to rest for at least three hours after the Rumble Ball effect had subsided. When exhausted, one cannot use their powers properly and must regain strength.

Devil Fruit powers can, in rare instances, achieve , significantly increasing the user's abilities. According to Kaidou, awakening occurs when a Devil Fruit user's mind and body catch up to their powers. When a Devil Fruit's power is awakened, the increased abilities have been seen to allow significantly greater power, more refined control, and new abilities that would otherwise not be possible. The effects of the awakening depend on the type of Devil Fruit. Awakening was first mentioned by Crocodile in the Impel Down Arc.

Furthermore, through Awakening it becomes possible to assert Devil Fruit powers over Haki, even overcoming the Haki of entities that was otherwise so strong that the fruit's effects largely washed right off of its user, with one instance showing that even a Supreme King and an Armament-clad blow from one of the Four Emperors were unable to completely ignore the body modifications bestowed by the fruit in question after it had awakened.
It has been noted that it takes time to fully master awakened powers; if not fully mastered, their usage will take a serious toll on the user's stamina.

Paramecia Awakening For Paramecias, an Awakening allows the user to use their Devil Fruits at a new level of strength and in different manners than they originally could. Luffy, upon seeing the Awakened power of the Ito Ito no Mi, commented that it did not seem like that of a mere Paramecia.
thumb|210px|Doflamingo uses the Ito Ito no Mi to turn the environment into strings.

An Awakened Paramecia allows the user to spread their power beyond their own body and transform or alter the properties of the material environment around them to match the nature of their Devil Fruit power, as well as manipulate the transformed material in any way they desire. The transformation effect can be spread over an extensive area. The main difference between an Awakening and the initial state of a Paramecia's abilities when first consuming the Devil Fruit, such as the Hira Hira no Mi, is that Awakening allows one to transform the environment from afar, as well as control it with just their mind, whereas unawakened Paramecias require the user to touch what they wish to transform and often require bodily movement to be controlled.

For example, after Doflamingo achieved the Awakening of the Ito Ito no Mi, he became able to extend the potency of his string-creating ability, transmuting the ground and buildings into vast quantities of string that he can manipulate without even the need to touch them. Katakuri similarly affected the environment with the Awakened Mochi Mochi no Mi during his battle with Luffy, causing the walls of the Mirro-World to behave like and even become edible like mochi. The non-canon villain Douglas Bullet was able to Awaken the power of the Gasha Gasha no Mi, allowing him to extend the range of his power to disassemble and restructure entire islands to his liking.

That being said, the ability to transform and manipulate foreign objects remotely is not universal, with a few abilities showcasing unique particularities despite the general idea of property alteration still being present. After Awakening the Jiki Jiki no Mi, Eustass Kid became capable of magnetizing things other than his own body, even other living beings, causing them to strongly attract and be buried under mountains of metal. Similarly, the Awakening of Trafalgar Law's Ope Ope no Mi allowed him to alter the properties of foreign objects to turn them into small space-defying ROOMs in essence, though the application process of this enhanced power is done manually.

In addition, both Kid and Law have insinuated that using the advanced powers granted by Awakening takes a huge toll on their bodies due to the high energy consumption to perform, turning those techniques into last resorts meant to finish off opponents. It is unknown if this applies to every Paramecia's Awakening or is a particularity of their individual Fruits.

Furthermore, aside from great environmental range, Awakened Paramecias may even provide entirely new abilities to their users. For example, Kid can apply inverse magnetic polarities to different non-metallic objects to make them strongly attract each other, completely bypassing the need to manipulate metal, which was the Jiki Jiki no Mi's primary application pre-Awakening. The non-canon villain Gild Tesoro, upon Awakening the Goru Goru no Mi, was able to create a complex sensory network out of the gold he touched, enabling him to sense the movements of all his gold down to individual coins and even gold ground down to a fine powder.
Zoan Awakening thumb|left|210px|The four Jailer Beasts are failed awakened Zoans whose minds were consumed by their powers.

For Zoan-type powers, awakening grants far greater strength, speed, and durability than un-awakened Zoan powers. This array of abilities also includes faster recovery time, which functions involuntarily, even when the user is unconscious.

Zoan Awakenings come with a great risk where the innate nature of the Zoan will consume the user's personality, turning them into simpleminded man-beasts. An example of this is the Jailer Beasts of Impel Down; they have yet to show any signs of complex thought, seemingly acting out on instinct and power, and they are always in a form resembling their full beast form, but with human attributes. It is unknown if they lost themselves and became this way permanently upon awakening or if they retain enough sentience that these forms are a conscious choice.
thumb|210px|The Five Elders are successfully awakened Mythical Zoans who retain their personalities.

As seen with Rob Lucci and Kaku, however, not all Zoan users lose themselves upon awakening. In such cases, they may even attain a new, powerful transformation known as that is divine in appearance, signified by a sash of flaming smoke that is usually black in color. Such a successful awakening is considered rare.

Not much is known about Mythical Zoan awakenings other than information shared with standard Zoan awakenings. So far all Mythical Zoan awakenings have been successful, leaving the user's personality intact; notably, however, the Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika, affects their personality in other ways, causing them to be overwhelmed with joy.

How a Mythical Zoan's unique abilities are affected by awakening is unclear. In the case of the Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika, the user gains the ability to freely alter the shape and size of their rubbery body however they wish. Furthermore, they gain the power to extend their rubber body powers to surrounding non-living materials, similar to how certain awakened Paramecia-type powers affect the environment. However, this is considered unusual by Kaidou.

Devil Fruits and the World Because encounters with Devil Fruits are rare (especially outside the Grand Line), various rumors have grown around them, making it difficult to tell between fact or fiction; some dismissed Devil Fruits as mere myths until actually getting to see one in action. The average person knows nothing or very little about what they are or what they do; this especially applies to people in isolated countries, even within the Grand Line, such as the people of Wano Country and even Princess Shirahoshi of Fish-Man Island, as none of them know about Devil Fruits. Instead, they believe the powers bestowed to users are curses or sorcery. Relatedly, Devil Fruits may also lead to the user being considered a "freak" and treated as an outcast. This treatment is due to some of the abilities considered far too strange or frightening for normal people to accept.
thumb|left|210px|The Big Mom Pirates, one of the strongest organizations in the world, consists of many Devil Fruit users.

They are relatively common in the Grand Line compared to the four blues. Many pirate crews in the Grand Line are centered around a captain with Devil Fruit powers (as with the Bellamy Pirates, the Bliking Pirates, or the Foxy Pirates), with the most predominant crews and organizations almost inevitably containing multiple Devil Fruit users (as with the Whitebeard Pirates, the Big Mom Pirates, the Beasts Pirates, the Straw Hat Pirates, the Donquixote Pirates, Baroque Works, or the Marines). Two Emperors (Blackbeard and Kaidou) have gone out of their way to gather as many Devil Fruits as possible using their unique methods.

Because of their power, Devil Fruits are highly sought after by many interests and organizations around the world, including the government and the Underworld. If sold, a typical specimen can expect to fetch well over 100,000,000, and Devil Fruit users themselves are sold at market prices the same way slaves are. Of course, Devil Fruits identified with especially desirable powers can easily boast even higher prices: the Ope Ope no Mi, reputed to grant immortality, is worth over 5,000,000,000 on the black market.
Knowledge and Documentation thumb|210px|The Devil Fruit Encyclopedia owned by the Vinsmoke Family.

There are at least two versions of a that identify Devil Fruits. The only known information about the old Devil Fruit Encyclopedia is that it has no mention of the Gomu Gomu no Mi, according to Vegapunk. The newer version lists the names and powers of all the Devil Fruits. However, only a few have illustrations, meaning that most Devil Fruits cannot be identified by their appearance. For example, the Gomu Gomu no Mi and the Yami Yami no Mi had supplementary pictures and could be recognized before consumption, whereas the Awa Awa no Mi and the Ushi Ushi no Mi, Model: Giraffe, do not and could only be identified by the abilities they granted.

One individual known to utilize this book is Blackbeard, who, in his search for the Yami Yami no Mi, memorized its shape from the illustration provided. The Vinsmoke Family also has a copy of the encyclopedia, which Sanji read, causing him to become interested in the Suke Suke no Mi. A third copy of the encyclopedia was present in the Sorbet Kingdom and was used by a resident to identify the Toshi Toshi no Mi's abilities.

Myths and Misconceptions Due to the rarity and mysterious nature of the Devil Fruits, many rumors surround their existence. Especially remote regions of the four cardinal Blues or isolated nations such as Wano Country often lack even basic knowledge of the fruits, believing them to be entirely mythical or attributing their powers to pure magic. The following is a list of various myths and misconceptions about Devil Fruits in the world.

As stated by Shanks, Devil Fruit are considered by some to be of the . Jabra believed a rumor that Devil Fruit users housed actual devils inside them. According to the rumor, if a Devil Fruit user went near an uneaten Devil Fruit, a devil would come out of the fruit and rip the user apart. This rumor has been debunked by research. In Amazon Lily, the citizens are unaware of the existence of Devil Fruits. The ruling Gorgon Sisters are believed to have gained their Mero Mero no Mi and Hebi Hebi no Mi abilities from a curse cast by a creature known as the "Gorgon". Vander Decken IX refers to his Mato Mato no Mi ability as the "Mato Mato Curse". Sugar's Hobi Hobi no Mi is also called the "Hobi Hobi Curse" by its victims. The Tontatta Tribe of Green Bit refer to Devil Fruit abilities as . In Wano Country, Devil Fruit abilities are considered or Ninjutsu. Devil Fruit users are called .

Fruits with Special Titles Certain Devil Fruits are noted to be unique or special, even for their respective types. Such include: The Goro Goro no Mi, which has been deemed as one of the few "invincible" Devil Fruits, though Luffy was able to counteract it with his rubbery physiology. The Yami Yami no Mi, which has been claimed to be "unique", even for a Logia. Teach even stated that it was the "true power of the Devil" and is the most evil of all Devil Fruits. The Gura Gura no Mi, which has been called the strongest Paramecia, is equal to a Logia. Sengoku stated that it was powerful enough to destroy the world. The Magu Magu no Mi, which is stated to be one of the highest offensive powers among all Devil Fruits. The Ope Ope no Mi, which has been called the "Ultimate Devil Fruit" due to its ability to grant eternal life. The Mochi Mochi no Mi, which was first introduced as a Logia in the Weekly Shonen Jump release, would later be identified in Volume 86 as a "special" Paramecia by Jinbe. The Hito Hito no Mi, Model: Nika, which has been referred to as the most ridiculous power in the world. The Ryu Ryu no Mi, Model: Nidhöggr, which has been passed down through the royal bloodline of Elbaph, has been called a "Legendary Devil Fruit."

Scientific Research and Developments Dr. Vegapunk, a Marine scientist said to be the world’s leading expert on Devil Fruits, is heavily responsible for researching the effects and origins of Devil Fruits, as well as their interactions with Seastone. Vegapunk was the one who discovered that Devil Fruits work by affecting the Lineage Factor.

Caesar Clown stated that he has done numerous experiments on his own Devil Fruit, insinuating that he managed to enhance its power after consumption. He has not yet explained his research or how he did it.
Drugs Some Devil Fruit users have invented certain drugs that can alter and/or enhance their powers. So far, this has only been seen with Zoan users.

Tony Tony Chopper, during his six-year tutelage under Dr. Kureha, created a special drug called the Rumble Ball. It temporarily modifies the effects of his Devil Fruit by "disrupting the wavelength" to create new forms outside the default three.

Though the Rumble Ball takes effect immediately on consumption, it has always carried side-effects and limitations. The original formula was effective for only three minutes, and needed six-hour intervals between uses. A second Rumble Ball within this timeframe would completely randomize Chopper's control over the transformations, while a third would transform him into a mindless, nigh-unstoppable giant creature that would attack friend and foe alike, drain his energy to potentially lethal levels, and have no reversion method except outright Devil Fruit nullification, e.g., seawater. Once he returned to his normal form, he would be completely exhausted and unable to move for several hours.

After two years of training and research on an island with incredible medical knowledge, Chopper learned how to access most of the Rumble Ball's additional forms without actually taking the drug. Whenever he does take it, he then transforms into the monstrous form that he previously turned into by taking three Rumble Balls in a short time, which he was since able to gain full mental control over. As before, the transformation lasts only three minutes, and the aftereffects still leave him paralyzed for several hours.

Later still, with Caesar Clown's help, Chopper extended the Rumble Ball's effect to last 30 minutes. However, the aftereffect that follows suit will be that Chopper will temporarily regress to a tiny form and take on an "old geezer" mentality.

Black Maria was able to alter the appearance of her Devil Fruit's Human-Beast form via drugs; instead of turning into an anthropomorphic beast person, she takes on a more centaur-like form. This also affected the spider portion of her transformation, granting it a separate face from Black Maria. The reason Black Maria decided to change her transformations appearance was not for combat purposes, but rather because she felt that her natural hybrid form was not "beautiful".
Fruit-Powered Objects thumb|210px|Funkfreed, a sword powered by an elephant Zoan.

Some years before the current timeline, Dr. Vegapunk discovered a technique that allows inanimate objects (such as a gun or a sword) to "eat" a Devil Fruit. Its actual details and mechanics have not yet been revealed; thus far, only Zoan-type fruits have been seen employing it. The technique is evidently not limited to solid materials, as toxic gaseous slime can also be used as a medium.

Objects that have "eaten" a Zoan Fruit gain the standard Full Beast and Hybrid transformations, as well as the ability to revert to their object form at will. This gives them the mobility, abilities, and intelligence of the animal they turn into, in addition to having the properties and abilities of the object they were made from. Inanimate object Zoans seem to be very loyal to their owners. However, the object also gains a living creature's ability to feel pain and fear, and susceptibility to disease.

Notably, the teapot Bunbuku in Wano Country was also able to gain a fruit power and come to life, even though most of Wano is very primitive and closed off from the outside world. In a similar way, the legendary warhammer Ragnir from the island of Elbaph was able to consume a Devil Fruit several centuries ago and still remains conscious without visible deterioration or aging, implying that objects given consciousness and life by a Devil Fruit have a very long or unlimited longevity. Ragnir having been alive since the Void Century meant the methods of Devil Fruits being "fed" to objects was actually discovered long before Vegapunk officially recorded it.
In the non-canon Fischer's x One Piece - Search for the 7 Treasures, a Devil Fruit "consumed" by an object was shown to remain intact, with a single bite taken out of it.

As scientific research on Devil Fruits advanced, it became possible for artificial Devil Fruits to be created. Like real Devil Fruits, they grant powers to the consumer and take away their ability to swim. So far, two scientists, Dr. Vegapunk and Caesar Clown, have managed to synthesize and replicate Zoan Devil Fruits, though with different methods. Vegapunk used the Lineage Factors of preexisting Devil Fruit users to replicate their powers, whereas Caesar used Lineage Factors from animals to create artificial Zoan fruits; they are called SMILEs.

While the Zoan Fruits created by Vegapunk seem to replicate Zoan powers accurately (if with unnatural colorations), the SMILE fruits created by Caesar allow the eater to permanently take on an animal attribute or body part(s). Furthermore, the SMILEs have a severe flaw: only 10% of the people who eat them could attain an animal power, while the remaining 90%, in addition to not gaining any powers, will lose not just their ability to swim, but also their ability to express any emotions other than joy, forcing them to constantly smile and laugh no matter what their true feelings.

The manufacturing process of SMILE Fruits involved having luminescent sunflowers provide light to the trees growing the fruits while SAD is poured into a river leading into irrigation canals which then channel the river under the trees to feed them the chemical.

It should be noted that only Zoan-type fruits can be created artificially. Paramecia fruits cannot be created, however, the powers themselves can be replicated as long as the original users bloodline elements are available. These copied powers can be given to a recipient through artificial Green Blood. Logia fruit powers have proven too difficult to replicate, although Vegapunk did manage to replicate the effects of the Pika Pika no Mi to a degree by developing functional laser weapons.

Early Concepts In Eiichiro Oda's first and second Romance Dawn prototypes, the Gomu Gomu no Mi was depicted near-identically to its counterpart in One Piece proper. However, both prototypes gave their origins as a that appeared once every fifty years, with no implications of similar or related fruits.

There have been several Devil Fruits, or Devil Fruit names, that were conceptualized but eventually cut from the series. Inazuma was initially meant to have a Crab-Zoan Devil Fruit before it was decided that he would have the Choki Choki no Mi. Marguerite was initially meant to have a Black Cat model of the Neko Neko no Mi series until it was decided that she would not have a Devil Fruit. Initially, Katakuri was going to have the "Kona Kona no Mi", a Logia that allows the user to transform into flour, before it was changed to the Mochi Mochi no Mi. Smoothie's Devil Fruit was going to be called the "Kaju Kaju no Mi" or the "Shiru Shiru no Mi" before it was decided to call it the Shibo Shibo no Mi. Black Maria was initially meant to have an Ancient Zoan Devil Fruit that would turn her into a stegosaurus, and then was going to have a Paramecia-type Devil Fruit known as the "Obi Obi no Mi" before it was decided for her to have the Kumo Kumo no Mi, Model: Rosamygale Grauvogeli.

Translation and Dub Issues Many Devil Fruits are named after highly specific Japanese concepts and (or shortenings thereof), rendering direct translations awkward if not impossible. For instance, the Mera Mera no Mi is named for the "crackling" sounds of a fire; all official English translations name it after synonyms for fire itself.

The 4Kids-dubbed anime renames the fruits to "Cursèd Fruits" (pronounced as two distinct syllables) to avoid religious implications. This is not observed by any other translation (though in the Funimation dub, Corto uniquely calls them "Diablo Fruit").
Incidentally, "Devil Fruit" is printed in English on at least one copy of the Devil Fruit Encyclopedia.

Trivia During the time of the Thriller Bark Arc, an SBS column stated that a "certain professor" would explain the true nature of Devil Fruits. This professor was generally expected to be Vegapunk, who did explain his views on the origin of Devil Fruits in the Egghead Arc; however, this explanation was only a theory and did not address many of the long-standing mysteries around Devil Fruits, like why the same fruit power cannot exist more than once at a time. Oda has yet to confirm if Vegapunk was indeed the "professor" he was referring to. Vegapunk's theory on the origin of the Devil Fruits has much in common with fellow scientist Willie Gallon's seemingly famous phrase in the Jaya Arc that "anything that man can imagine is a possibility in reality." According to Pell, exist in the world. It remains unknown what metric this relied on, or if it was ever meant to be accurate to the wider story. Though Marshall D. Teach is so far the only person to outright hold two Devil Fruit powers, there have been other instances where a Devil Fruit user was able to copy and/or utilize the ability of another user through their own ability, but only by the extent their own ability will allow. Charlotte Brûlée can use other Devil Fruit powers while mirroring another user: when mirroring Luffy and Caesar, she was able to mimic their rubber and gas powers almost perfectly. Jewelry Bonney's Toshi Toshi no Mi, particularly her Distortion Future technique, allows her to age herself into a possible future where she has the rubbery properties of Nika, thereby gaining the powers of the Gomu Gomu no Mi. Bentham's Mane Mane no Mi allows him to shapeshift into Tony Tony Chopper's hybrid form, an otherwise-unique product of the Hito Hito no Mi (though, curiously, with Bentham's natural height). In the 9th movie, Wapol devoured and merged with his brother Musshuru and thus was able to combine Musshuru's poisonous spore powers with his own. An art oversight in Chapter 175 depicted Galdino clearly floating on water, despite his Devil Fruit power. While the corresponding anime episode simply added a table beneath him; a later SBS column jokingly claimed that he had been propped up by a small piece of "super-floaty wood" (which an even later column retroactively deemed Kuuigosu). A similar oversight would also affect Bellamy during his ring out in the Corrida Colosseum in Chapter 709, with the corresponding anime episode correcting it by adding some rubble underneath him. Masked Deuce is the only known eater of a naturally powerless Devil Fruit—the Mera Mera no Mi, which Portgas D. Ace had already taken the first bite of. Some Devil Fruits that can create additional foods—such as the Fude Fude no Mi and Kuku Kuku no Mi—apparently pass on their bad taste to said foods by default. The swirl patterns on Devil Fruits may be inspired by , a type of Japanese scroll design popularly used on furoshiki wrapping cloths; these cloths are, in turn, stereotypically associated with both market produce (including fruits) and thieves. The design concepts for Devil Fruits appear to have been deliberately changed around the time of the Dressrosa Arc: while all prior fruits were given relatively mundane designs, those from the Mera Mera no Mi and Ope Ope no Mi (shaped, respectively, after a flame and a heart) on have almost always been designed to reflect their powers, especially if profiled in One Piece Magazine. Interestingly, an inability to swim was common to real-life sailors—including pirates—in pre-modern times, and some nautical superstitions openly discouraged learning it. Modern authorities ascribe this to a combination of such sailors having mostly inland backgrounds, and the fatalistic belief that men overboard could not expect rescue (so swimming could only prolong their suffering). The rumor that Jabra recounted about Devil Fruits housing actual devils is similar to the Hindu belief about ; because of this, the Hindus of Northern India avoid the trees and will not sit in their shade. However, Beleric fruit is also known for its medicinal properties and is used by Hindu physicians for various ailments. The other part of Jabra's rumor about the fruit's devil tearing out and killing the consumer from within is similar to other Hindu legends, particularly the , about two rakshasa brothers: would take the shape of a fruit or meat and would offer the "food" to innocent mendicants passing by. Vatapi would come out by tearing through the victim's body. However, this failed against .

SBS-Based Trivia In an SBS published shortly after Wapol's introduction, a reader asked if they could get Luffy's Gomu Gomu no Mi powers by eating him. Oda answered that the reader would get food poisoning. Oda explained in an SBS why he made it so Devil Fruit powers extend through the users' clothing. He said that if he had done it realistically, the manga would have had too much unnecessary nudity. Nonetheless, some Devil Fruits explicitly do not affect the user's or victim's clothing, such as the Toshi Toshi no Mi. Many SBS questions have concerned whether various Devil Fruits (including the Gomu Gomu no Mi, Bara Bara no Mi, Hana Hana no Mi, and Hie Hie no Mi) extend their powers to the user's genitals. In every known case, Oda has answered yes. According to Oda, Devil Fruits are one of the few aspects of the One Piece anime that he has relatively complete control over; the anime's writers must request his permission to introduce an anime-original ability, and he may refuse if he already has the same idea for a manga story. It is unknown whether this also holds for more tertiary media, such as video games and stage shows. Notably, there are two Devil Fruits with the name Nori Nori no Mi that bestow different powers; the non-canon version appeared first in the 2021 Premier Show, while the canon fruit debuted in 2023. Oda claimed in One Piece Blue's Q&A column (ca. 2002) that if he could eat any Devil Fruit, it would be Buggy's Bara Bara no Mi. However, in Volume 62's SBS (ca. 2011) he implied it would be Absalom's Suke Suke no Mi. A Q&A from the July 2010 issue of the North American Weekly Shonen Jump claimed that Oda most wanted to be Nico Robin so he could use the Hana Hana no Mi to draw faster. Though this was sourced to an interview from 2008's Jump Festa, no Japanese corroboration or documentation is known to exist. According to Oda, he originally did not intend to include a fruit like the Fuwa Fuwa no Mi in the canon and was only willing to use the ability in a movie. This was because he felt that an ability for limitless flight would not fit a story about pirates. However, due to Shiki being a canon character, Oda admits that the Fuwa Fuwa no Mi too must now be considered canon. Shiki later demonstrated the ability in Chapter 1157. This may explain Pell's claim of there being only five "confirmed" flight powers in the world early in the series.

The Gunyo Gunyo no Mi is an unknown-type Devil Fruit that allows the user to create and control clay, making the user a . It was eaten by Prince Grus.
Etymology is a Japanese onomatopoeia for a soft, pliable substance (like clay) being squished. The VIZ manga and Crunchyroll subs, it is called the Glorp-Glorp Fruit.

A user of this fruit's power can generate clay from their body and mold it into different shapes akin to . This includes the creation of human-like, animated figures called "golems" that can fight on the user's behalf, being invulnerable to damage. It seems that the ability's user can freely alter the hardness of the clay, from creating large massses of soft, mushy clay to making smaller, hardened constructs to wield as weapons.
No weaknesses of this ability are known apart from the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses.

Usage thumb|210px|Grus wielding a clay-made morning star. Grus uses the clay he creates for offensive, defensive, and auxiliary purposes. He chiefly uses his power to create animated golems that fight for him while he can stay out of harm's way, observing at a safe distance. He can manipulate clay in its soft state (such as summoning large, shapeless masses to cushion a ship's fall onto land) or harden clay to fashion solid weapons to wield by hand (e.g., a spiked morning star), or large defensive structures.

Applications : An ability that involves Grus forming realistically human-looking figures out of clay; it is unknown to what degree these golems possess sentience/autonomy, though they are capable of fighting on their own and even speaking. Being made of clay, they are invulnerable to conventional attacks like gunfire and, upon taking damage, will reform from clay in a Logia-like fashion. Grus seems to keep three golems as his signature entourage, in the form of three hulking men.

Techniques thumb|210px|Grus using Nyudo Gunyo. : A technique where Grus calls forth a massive, cushiony wave of clay to cover the ground in front of him. He was first seen using the move to soften the fall of Monkey D. Garp's airborne ship onto the island of Hachinosu. The technique's name is a pun on , a Japanese word for "cumulonimbus", referencing the cloud-like appearance of the claybed that is created (with nyūdō being a term that refers to someone entering Buddhist priesthood). In the VIZ manga and Crunchyroll adaptations, this technique is called Cumulo-Glorpus.

thumb|210px|Grus using Gunyo no Su. : A defensive technique where Grus brings forth an enormous clay net shaped like a spiderweb, with which he can block out incoming threats. He was seen using the net to catch falling pieces of rubble created when Koby destroyed Avalo Pizarro's massive "island" arm in the air above Garp's ship, the clay wrapping around the debris as it fell into the sea. The technique's name phonetically resembles . In the VIZ manga and Crunchyroll adaptations, this technique is called Glorp Web.

Trivia In Jewish folklore, a is a humanoid figure artificially constructed from clay or mud and endowed with life by magical means (like a spell or Kabbalistic rite involving a piece of paper, inscribed with Hebrew words, being inserted into the golem's mouth). It is currently unknown whether this fruit is a Paramecia or Logia. Clay is a naturally occurring substance and the golems created by Grus were compared to Logia users, but it is unknown whether Grus himself can transform into clay. The official One Piece website lists Prince under Paramecia users. Grus' golem-creating ability is reminiscent of Charlotte Cracker's Bisu Bisu no Mi power, which likewise involves the creation of human-like beings from inanimate matter (in this case biscuit material). In Cracker's case though, his Biscuit Soldiers were not sentient on their own. Additionally, while Cracker must first clap his hands to make his biscuits appear, Grus seems to have to, or mainly does, produce clay from the palms of his hands without any gesture involved. During the Marineford Arc, the pirate Elmy used an unnamed ability to control a massive golem of sorts, made from a clay-like substance and thus resembling this fruit's power (though such resemblance is lost in the anime). Grus' Gunyo no Su technique resembles Doflamingo's string-based Kumo no Sugaki technique.

Logia is one of the three Devil Fruit types, being the rarest (discounting "Mythical Zoans") and most powerful. Someone wielding a Logia power can transform their body into an element of nature at will, as well as create and control vast amounts of that element.
The term Logia was first used when Raki heard about Enel's Devil Fruit abilities.

Etymology (λογία), plural of lógion (λόγιον), is an ancient Greek word originating from religious scholarship and roughly translating as "sayings, utterances, oracles," in reference to communications of divine origin, such as sayings attributed to Jesus in the Gospels. The suffix -logíā (Greek: -λογῐ́ᾱ) from lógos (λόγος, "word") is a base for nouns denoting the study of something (a disciplinary branch of knowledge). Latinized as -logia, it has been adapted into English as (e.g., theology).
Overview thumb|210px|left|Crocodile's sand-made Logia body is invulnerable, with regular attacks simply disrupting his shape.

Compared to the Paramecia and Zoan Devil Fruits, those with Logia powers can physically transform into a particular element of nature, on top of creating that element from their body in nigh-endless quantities to control as they please. The transformative aspect of Logias serves to distinguish them from other Devil Fruit types, particularly Paramecia abilities that allow for the generation of substances: such Paramecias only allow one to create—not become—one's respective substance, barring one known exception denoted as "special" for its kind. All canon Logia powers pertain to elements that are raw and naturally occurring while behaving as they would in nature (whereas substance-creating Paramecias involve man-made materials that sometimes exhibit unnatural, esoteric properties). Logia elements may come in all major states of matter, including solids, liquids, gases, and plasmas, as well as energy.

Bodies transformed by a Logia ability are completely invulnerable to most attacks, as when they are hit and thus blown out of shape, they will simply reform without any damage, and seemingly automatically at that. This applies to both blunt and sharp-force damage, as well as severed limbs and decapitation. It is unclear how much conscious control is required to transform one's body to negate attacks; while no Logia user has ever shown difficulty or the inability to bypass attacks, there have been instances of forceful contact with a user's real body and of unwilling transformation into their element. While some Logia types grant elemental bodies that, though invulnerable and capable of seamless regeneration, are still solid (e.g., ice and wood) or at least substantive, those Logias based on gaseous, plasmic, or energy-based elements are wholly "intangible" in practical terms (though their form may still potentially be disrupted by attacks).

There are a few ways to negate the invulnerability granted by Logia abilities and successfully injure a transformed Logia user, including the standard Devil Fruit weaknesses to seawater and Seastone, which prevent the user from accessing their Devil Fruit abilities. All Logia fruits also have a weakness to Armament Haki, as they can be injured by an opponent using this Haki. Certain Logia fruits also have individual weaknesses, which reflect the element's natural vulnerabilities. Such instances include liquids such as water cancelling out sand, electrical insulators such as rubber cancelling out lightning, and magma cancelling out fire.

In order to generate their substance, a Logia user must first transform part of their body into the substance, which then multiplies as they please; this differs from substance-generating Paramecia users, most of whom can generate substances directly from their physical body or even from thin air. As long as the reproducing substance is attached to the user's body, it is considered part of their body, though it appears that this is no longer the case once the user splits it off. If they encounter their substance in nature, a Logia user can merge with it, and the natural substance will become part of their body as well.

The Yami Yami no Mi is a special Logia fruit unlike others. Its darkness transformation is not founded in a naturally occurring element, but rather takes the form of a black smoke that most closely resembles the darkness of a . The user cannot render themselves invulnerable to enemy attacks, as black holes absorb all things that approach them. Instead, the user has the ability to nullify other users' Devil Fruit powers, as they can simply absorb their enemy's abilities.

Logia fruits are considered to be the strongest among the three basic Devil Fruit types, with the most powerful Paramecia, the Gura Gura no Mi, being compared to a Logia in terms of potency. As Logias grant the ability to create near-endless amounts of an element and thus control forces of nature, just about every Logia user has immense offensive and destructive power at their disposal, akin to a concentrated natural disaster. Fire and magma transformations can instantly burn opponents, lightning can electrocute opponents with a single hit, and light can blind opponents and pierce through them like lasers. The Gasu Gasu no Mi can create a large variety of gases, many of which are toxic or explosive and can cause instant death; it is also capable of removing oxygen from the air. The user of the Hie Hie no Mi can flash-freeze people, while the Yuki Yuki no Mi user can give people hypothermia by surrounding them in snow. People who get caught in the swamp made by the Numa Numa no Mi will be trapped in it, the user of the Mori Mori no Mi can effectively turn into a forest of deadly flora, and the darkness of the Yami Yami no Mi can pull in any object and crush it to smithereens.
thumb|left|210px|When Kuzan's ice and Sakazuki's magma clashed for ten days, they permanently altered Punk Hazard's climate.

In addition to their potency against opponents in a fight, the elements that Logia users transform into can also have a significant effect on their surrounding environment, from the land and water around them to even the climate. This was notably seen on Punk Hazard, where a ten-day battle between Magu Magu no Mi user Sakazuki and Hie Hie no Mi user Kuzan caused half of the island to become a hot, fiery land and the other half to become a cold, snowy land. Additionally, Crocodile was able to use the Suna Suna no Mi to create massive sandstorms in the desert country Arabasta, and Kuzan can travel across the ocean by freezing it. The ability of Logia users to merge with their element means that certain locations make particular Logia users stronger, such as the desert for the Suna Suna no Mi user and gaseous environments for the Gasu Gasu no Mi user. If Logia users are given enough time, their attacks can impact and even destroy areas on an unprecedented scale. Thus, most Logia-type users are capable of unleashing powerful and large-scale attacks rivaled by few. Notable example of Logia users' mass destruction capabilities includes Blackbeard pulling an entire town inside him with the Yami Yami no Mi, as well as Enel completely obliterating Angel Island (and planning to obliterate all of Skypiea) with the Goro Goro no Mi.

Defensively, the intangibility of Logia users when transformed makes them extremely difficult, if not impossible, to harm, let alone defeat. Unless one has learned Armament Haki (a skill which is not common outside the New World), or has managed to acquire an element to cancel out a Logia user's power, it is near impossible to injure a Logia user. The Tsumegeri Guards of Arabasta, who had no knowledge of Armament Haki, were at a loss for how to injure Crocodile, with the only options they could think of being the consumption of Hero Water to grow physically stronger, which in no way impacted his sand intangibility. On Skypiea, Enel was able to toy with Kamakiri for five minutes by doing nothing but sitting and transforming to render the warrior's constant attacks useless.
thumb|left|210px|Monet in her fluid snow form dodges a Haki-imbued attack from Tashigi.

Fully transforming their body into an element gives Logia users several advantages, one of those being the ability to disguise themselves by becoming part of their environment. Additionally, fully transformed users are capable of freely manipulating their body's shape at will. Karasu uses his ability to divide up his body into a murder of crows made of compressed soot. These birds carry Karasu's consciousness (seeing as they are made from his body) and can serve various tasks such as attacking or disarming enemies, and outside of combat by, for instance, receiving and relaying information or transporting objects or people. As shown by Kuzan and Monet, skilled Logia users can utilize this ability to morph their elemental bodies out of the way of attacks that would actually physically damage them, even to the point of opening full-fledged holes in their own body, so that their enemies attack would just pass harmlessly through empty air. Charlotte Katakuri, whose fruit is classified as a Paramecia but has the same abilities as a Logia, has perfected this skill with Observation Haki to foresee opponents' attacks and transform parts of his body into mochi to shift out of the way accordingly.

Additionally, Logia users can use their element to aid their physical bodies, such as when Enel used his lightning to jumpstart his stopped heart. Users who transform into elements that are lighter than air are capable of flight by transforming the lower half of their body. Logia users have also used their abilities to power machines and objects with their elements. This has been seen with Smoker using smoke to power his Billower Bike, Ace using fire to power his Striker raft, Enel using lightning to power the Ark Maxim, and Caesar Clown feeding gas into a sword hilt to create a flaming sword.

Despite the fearsome power of Logia users, they are not invincible. Overconfident Logia users who rely too much on their ability to avoid damage are often swiftly defeated when they encounter someone who can counter their abilities. Areas like the New World are full of experienced fighters who know a lot about Devil Fruit abilities and how to fight them.
thumb|left|210px|left|Luffy using Haki to make physical contact with Caesar Clown's gaseous body.

The most common way to bypass Logia protections is by using Armament Haki. Haki does not prevent Logia users from transforming or completely deactivate the transformation; rather, once a Haki-imbued object makes contact with a transformed body, the body part that is struck reverts to its solid form. Thus, a Logia user that is hit with a Haki-imbued attack in their transformed state will be harmed as if they had not transformed. Such properties also apply to Logias being grabbed by an user of Armament, best exemplified by Caesar being unable to shake off from Luffy's hold on him, forcing the former to forcefully attempt to strike back instead of simply splitting away and reforming. Being in a transformed state may cause the user to expand and occupy a larger surface area than their normal body would, allowing Haki-wielding opponents to strike and injure them with greater ease.

Additionally, Logia users may lose their intangibility when their bodies come into contact with an element that has a special reaction with their element. When struck by said element, they are affected in the same way as when they are hit by Armament Haki. For example, if the Suna Suna no Mi user comes into contact with a liquid, the sand will stick together or harden, thus forcing the user into a tangible state. Another example is when two Logia users clash and one element is naturally superior to the other, as seen when Sakazuki used his magma to injure Ace's fire body. Alternatively, two Logia elements may completely stalemate upon clashing, such as fire and smoke. Other examples of elements being used to cancel out a Logia user's power were when Monkey D. Luffy bypassed Crocodile's sand by coating his body with water, and later blood, as well as when Luffy bypassed Enel's lightning with just his body due to being made of rubber. Logia users may still be able to outlast and overpower opponents who can bypass their intangibility through intelligent use of their ability, like, for example, Crocodile using his dehydrating powers to directly absorb water attacks or Aramaki turning his wooden body fireproof, and they may also use Haki to protect themselves. Nonetheless, being able to bypass intangibility significantly improves a person's chances when fighting Logia users, and they may be able to take the Logia user off-guard, especially if the user is overconfident in their ability.

It is possible to trap a transformed Logia user in an enclosed space, especially if their element is solid, and render it difficult to impossible for them to escape. This was seen when the Straw Hat Pirates caught Caribou inside a barrel and bolted it shut, preventing him from escaping until someone else opened it later. Luffy attempted to defeat Crocodile by eating his transformed head and torso, which did disrupt the Warlord, although he was able to quickly burst out. Users with solid and rigid elemental transformations, such as ice, are slower to reform when their elemental bodies are attacked and damaged.

A Logia user may be unable to effectively perform and utilize their transformation if they are overwhelmed by an emotion such as fear. This was seen with Monet, who was gripped with fear after Roronoa Zoro bisected her without Haki and was unable to reform her body for a brief time.

Trivia Every canon Logia comes from a natural element, but some shown in non-canon media do come from man-made substances. Except for Enel, every canon Logia user that was revealed before the timeskip was present during the Summit War of Marineford. Trebol utilizes his Paramecia ability, the Beta Beta no Mi, to create a thick coat of mucus over his slim and frail body to trick his opponents into thinking he has a Logia ability. In the magazine release of Chapter 863, the Mochi Mochi no Mi was stated to be a Logia, but this has been changed in the volume release into a "special Paramecia". Katakuri was originally meant to have the powers of the Kona Kona no Mi, a Logia Devil Fruit that allowed him to turn into flour. However, considering that flour is a man-made substance and not a natural resource, this ability may have also been reclassified as "special Paramecia". The Marines currently hold the largest known number of Logia fruit users in a single organization, with 4 users (Smoker, Borsalino, Sakazuki and Aramaki) Additionally, they also had Kuzan before he resigned, and Caesar Clown before he was dismissed. Despite Vegapunk's best efforts, Logia is the only type of Devil Fruits he failed to artificially replicate due to their complexity. Thus far, Logia is the only Devil Fruit category with no known Awakened users, and the function of the category's awakenings is unknown. While Logia is considered the strongest of the three basic types of Devil Fruits, it has been suggested that the even more rare Mythical Zoan-type Devil Fruits might actually be more powerful. Despite Logia's being identified as more common, there are currently more Mythical Zoan fruits revealed than Logia fruits.
